hub.overview: The Hub separates opening an application, entering a project and managing shared work. A deep navy rail sits beside cool white working surfaces; cobalt marks selection and primary action. Existing application identities, dark ink and quiet status labels keep the local environment readable.
keyCharacteristics: Navy navigation, cool white surfaces and cobalt actions.
Six primary destinations with a labelled local tool selector.
Home pairs application launch rows with a project stack.
Authored navigation SVG and existing app icons; no new shipping raster imagery.

rules.name: The Hub Scope Rule
rules.body: Use the Hub workbench palette in hoard_link/hub/ui; keep the separate apps/agora amber console and its tokens scoped to that application.

dos: Do keep opening apps, entering projects and managing shared tools distinct, with every original tool reachable.
Do preserve full document scrolling, labelled local tool selection, wrapping and keyboard access.
Do treat projects as persistent Ágora spaces and preserve coordination workspace_url and space_id.
Do preserve unknown fields and invalid JSON while editing automation.
donts: Don't infer running apps or successful workspace availability from placeholders.
Don't add raster decoration or import the separate Ágora amber display typography.
Don't describe the navigation redesign as new backend, data or MCP capabilities.

references.description: Result rows and relation endpoints use native buttons; search has an accessible label and long URIs wrap.

chatSources.description: Sources and connections is a native details/summary disclosure so history remains the primary reading surface. Disabled sources retain full opacity with an explicit written state.

mail.drafts: Settings/status are hidden in reader. Unsaved configuration survives polling but hidden reader drafts are excluded from copilot pending_forms.
mail.errors: Loading and error/retry remain explicit. Same-sphere cached list survives transient loading failure.
mail.structure: One active Attention/Unclaimed/Recent queue, local filter, divided message list and full reader replace each other in document flow.
mail.returnState: Back preserves queue/category/query/page within the sphere and restores row focus. Sphere changes reset scope and invalidate superseded list/detail responses.
mail.dataScope: 20 rows per client page; requests up to40 Attention and100 Unclaimed from7 days, plus40 Recent. Search covers loaded subject, sender name/address and snippet, not server archive or full bodies.
mail.content: Text DOM renders paragraphs and simple headings. Only resolved HTTP/HTTPS URLs become links; attachments retain available labels/sizes. No message HTML interpretation.

narrative.overview:
Ágora extends the Hoard family's warm charcoal workspace into a full team console. A restrained amber wordmark anchors the frame, while quiet dividers make the three working areas legible: a permanent leader roster, a central group conversation and an operations pane. Source Sans 3 carries the information; Cinzel is reserved for the Ágora wordmark.

The surface favors named states, authorship and source details over decoration. The desktop keeps four leaders visible beside the conversation. At narrow widths, the leaders become a horizontal roster and operations open as a drawer; the conversation and composer remain the main work area. The visual system is a description of the shipped UI, not a claim that every provider workflow is complete.
keyCharacteristics: Warm charcoal surfaces with a focused amber accent.
Compact, divided work areas with a readable conversation measure.
Status, authorship and quota provenance are written out alongside color.
Provider state uses distinct restrained avatar colors; the wordmark remains the only display face.

rules.body: Reserve amber for the brand mark, primary action, focus and selected navigation; do not turn every leader or status into an amber accent.
rules.name: The Amber Signal Rule

rules.body: Cinzel appears in the wordmark; use Source Sans 3 for headings, messages, labels and controls.
rules.name: The One Display Face Rule

dos: Do use the warm charcoal, ivory and amber palette for the app frame and primary actions.
Do keep names and status words visible next to state color; unknown quota remains explicitly unknown rather than becoming a numeric zero.
Do preserve author, leader/helper identity and quota freshness in dense or narrow layouts.
Do keep the composer visually distinct and reachable while reading the conversation.
Do use visible keyboard focus and honor reduced-motion preferences.
donts: Don't add marketing slogans, hero metrics or decorative gradients to this operational surface.
Don't present mock activity or an unavailable provider as a live response.
Don't rely on color alone for connectivity, availability, quota or task state.
Don't spread the provider avatar tints across unrelated controls or panels.
